title: 5 More Critically Acclaimed Anime Crunchyroll Removed & You Can’t Stream Anywhere Else
content:
There’s no de

Crunchyroll is the largest streaming platform for anime fans across the world, home to over a thousand series and movies. Each year, the platform adds a few dozen new releases to make them more accessible for fans. This also means that a large number of series and films can be found on Crunchyroll, including older classics and the latest hits. However, it’s not rare for the platform to quietly remove some beloved shows without any announcement. These removals mostly happen due to licensing issues. Even though certain anime are exclusive to the platform, Crunchyroll only buys rights to stream them for a certain period of time.

Over time, the license expires, forcing the platform to remove such anime from its library. Additionally, while it’s possible for Crunchyroll to renew those licenses, it depends on the popularity of the anime. Regardless of critical acclaim, if an anime doesn’t have a good enough viewership, the platform would prefer to let them go. It hasn’t been long since these incredible anime were removed from Crunchyroll, and now fans in the U.S. can’t stream them anywhere.

5) Rokka: Braves of the Six Flowers

This is a rather underrated entry on the list, but the story is rather unique for an action fantasy. The anime never released a second season, and it might not return after the sudden removal from the platform. The story focuses on an ancient legend, with the revival of the Demon God, six heroes dubbed the Braves of the Six Flowers. These heroes will be chosen by the Goddess of Fate, granting them power to rise up against the fiends attempting to turn the world into a living hell.

Adlet Mayer, self-proclaimed Strongest Man in the World, becomes one of the chosen ones. The story continues as he embarks on a destined journey to fight the Demon God and meets up with the fellow heroes. However, things take a drastic turn when seven heroes are present instead of six, leading everyone to believe Adlet is a fraud. Now he must do everything he can to find the true imposter and fulfill his destiny of defeating the Demon God.

4) Grimgar, Ashes and Illusions

This underrated isekai is yet another series that never released a second season. It centers around a group of strangers who wake up in a mysterious fantasy world with no memories of their past lives. Unlike most isekai shows where the reincarnated or transmigrated characters adapt to their surroundings quickly, this anime doesn’t shy away from showing the brutal reality of being powerless and unprepared.

It’s a matter of survival for them as they’re only ordinary people thrust into a dangerous world where they must fight monsters for food and money. Their struggles are visceral and slow-paced, emphasizing the weight of every decision while they try to come out of this conundrum alive. The lack of overpowered characters and the fear of death makes the story deeply human, as the group relies on teamwork, trial and error, and bonds to survive.

3) Darker Than Black

Much like Noragami , Darker Than Black was forged thanks to Studio Bones, though this tale is far different from its predecessor earlier on the list. Focusing on covert agents known as “Contractors,” the anime adaptation got its start in 2007 with a full season of twenty-five episodes. It would then receive a sequel series in 2009, thanks to Darker Than Black: Gemini of Meteor , further expanding on its world. With the series also receiving a spin-off anime in 2010 of four episodes in Darker Than Black: Gaiden , the franchise is deserving of returning to the airwaves thanks to its unique storytelling style.

2) Orange

Even after more than a decade since its premiere, this time travel drama gets praise for its exceptional story and unique themes. While not a mainstream hit, the anime always had a dedicated fanbase, even if it’s been reduced over the past few years. The story centers around Naho Takamiya, whose first day of her sophomore year of high school takes a strange turn. She wakes up late and finds a mysterious letter addressed to her. However, she never expected that the letter was from herself 10 years in the future.

Although she is initially skeptical of the note, after witnessing several events described to take place, she realizes the letter really is from her 26-year-old self. The letter details Naho’s future full of regrets and hopes her younger self can correct the mistakes that were made in the past. With the knowledge of the future in her hands, she carefully makes decisions on what to do next in her life.

1) Akame Ga Kill

Since the manga ended two years after the anime, fans got a much better and happier conclusion than the anime. The animation studio completely ignored everything the manga did right and opted for a tragic conclusion with the death of the protagonist. However, he survives in the manga, even though he was transformed into a dragon-like creature due to overusing his Incursio armor. It’s not only Tatsumi, but even Mine survives and marries him.

Not only that, but even when a character’s fate didn’t deviate from the manga, the anime changed the events leading up to it, ruining its impact. The ending seems even more meaningless when none of the major characters actually live to see the rebellion’s victory, even if they fought so hard for it.

title: The Apothecary Diaries Is Getting a New Shojo Competitor Soon
content:
The Fall 2026 anime season is the biggest quarter of the year, and most of the credit goes to the return of major shows. This also includes The Apothecary Diaries Season 3, which has been growing in popularity ever since its premiere in 2023. While the light novel written by Natsu Hyuga has always been popular, the franchise became a massive worldwide success after the anime debut. Along with the TV anime series, the franchise also has a feature-length movie and a live-action series in the works . The premise of a young apothecary in the imperial palace isn’t as common as one might hope, which is all the more reason why The Apothecary Diaries stands out from the rest.

However, the anime industry is expanding every year with dozens of new series, and studio Doga Kobo recently released Though I Am an Inept Villainess , which had a lot of similar vibes . Following the anime’s success, another series with the same premise has been announced recently, which might be the next big thing Shojo fans will see. While The Apothecary Diaries is Seinen at its very core, the upcoming new anime will explore lighter themes due to its demographic. The Eccentric Doctor of the Moon Flower Kingdom also shared new updates while The Apothecary Diaries stays in the spotlight thanks to its latest season.

What Is The Eccentric Doctor of the Moon Flower Kingdom About?

Studio Elle, an underrated studio behind My Awkward Senpai, will be producing this upcoming anime. While the release date hasn’t been confirmed yet, the anime dropped its gorgeous first look last week, and it immediately drew attention thanks to the similarities it shared with The Apothecary Diaries . The anime is based on an ongoing manga by Tohru Himoka, who is also known for creating Shinobi Quartet and other underrated works. The story takes place in the Moon Flower Kingdom, where the people have only relied on superstition and dubious healing methods.

However, when Prince Keiun begins to search for more reliable remedies, his group is attacked by mysterious assailants. That was also when he encountered Koyou, an eccentric teenage girl who performed a lifesaving procedure that he had never witnessed in his entire life. His curiosity grows as he gets entangled with the girl while also dealing with the ones targeting him. The story features medical and political intrigue, mystery, romance, and basically everything The Apothecary Diaries fans can hope for .

The Apothecary Diaries Season 3 Is More Exciting Than Ever

There’s still a while before The Eccentric Doctor of the Moon Flower Kingdom will be released, but luckily The Apothecary Diaries Season 3 is airing its weekly episodes on Crunchyroll. The story continues after the rebellion of the Shi Clan, and just the opening is enough to tell you that the 12 episodes of the first cour will be more exciting than ever. Although Maomao doesn’t work at the Rear Palace anymore, she will continue to help Jinshi in solving mysteries happening all over the kingdom. Not to mention that the new season will also delve deeper into Jinshi’s origins and his role as the Moon Prince. Unlike the first two seasons, which ran for their two cours without breaks, Season 3 will be returning with its second part in April next year as part of the Spring 2027 lineup.

title: Tune in to the Midnight Heart Manga Goes on 1-Week Hiatus Due to Creator's Health
content:
This year's 45th issue of Kodansha 's Weekly Shōnen Magazine announced on Wednesday that Masakuni Igarashi 's Tune In to the Midnight Heart ( Mayonaka Heart Tune ) manga does not have a new chapter in the issue as initially planned, due to Igarashi getting sick. Igarashi is currently focused on recovering, and planning to resume the manga in the magazine's next issue on October 14.

Kodansha 's K MANGA service is publishing the manga digitally in English, and it describes the story:

When Arisu Yamabuki was all alone in bed at night, he was able to find solace in the voice of a radio host who went by “Apollo.” However, one day, she simply stopped broadcasting without any explanation. Years then passed, and Arisu is now a second-year high-schooler. He makes it his mission to search for Apollo, as there is something he wants to tell her. He doesn't know what she looks like, or even what her real name is, but he manages to get some leads on her in his school's broadcasting club. That's where he meets four girls who all dream to get a job where they can make full use of their voices! Just who is Apollo, and how will those four's dreams pan out?

Igarashi ( Senryū Girl , Detectives These Days Are Crazy! ) launched the manga in Kodansha 's Weekly Shōnen Magazine in September 2023. The 14th compiled book volume shipped on August 17. Kodansha USA Publishing licensed the manga and released the ninth volume on September 1.

The manga inspired a television anime that debuted on January 6. Crunchyroll streamed the anime, and it also streamed an English dub . The anime will have a second season that will premiere in 2027.

title: Kai-hen Wizards Manga to Publish 'Series Finale' on October 14
content:
This year's 45th issue of Shogakukan 's Weekly Shonen Sunday announced on Wednesday that Yellow Tanabe 's Kai-hen Wizards ( Kaihen no Mahōtsukai ) manga will publish its "series finale chapter" in the magazine's next issue on October 14. The expanded chapter will have 26 pages. The announcement does not specify if this is the overall final chapter of the manga, or simply the final chapter of an arc.

Viz Media releases the manga's English simultaneous publication, and describes the story:

A young boy must live in exile lest his deadly magical powers destroy the world.

Tanabe launched the series in Weekly Shonen Sunday in September 2024. Shogakukan published the manga's fourth compiled book volume on June 18.

The manga went on hiatus on February 9, and resumed on July 29.

Tanabe began serializing the Kekkaishi manga in Weekly Shonen Sunday in 2003 and ended it after eight years in 2011. The manga inspired a television anime that ran from 2006 to 2008. Viz Media released the anime in a set of four DVDs in 2011, and Discotek Media later released the anime on Blu-ray Disc in June 2022.

Tanabe launched the Birdmen manga in Weekly Shonen Sunday in July 2013, and ended it in February 2020.

title: 10 Years Ago Today, Jujutsu Kaisen Studio Premiered an Anime That Saved Its Future Before Its Cancellation
content:
Established in 2011, the renowned animation studio MAPPA eventually became one of the biggest in the industry after creating famous shows such as Jujutsu Kaisen and Chainsaw Man . However, 2016 was the breakthrough year for the studio after their sports anime, Yuri!!! on Ice became massively popular. The series premiered on October 6th, 2016, and followed a beautiful story of Yuri Katsuki, who does everything he can to strive for the top as a figure skater. The anime concluded on December 22nd of the same year before promising the story’s continuation. However, since it’s an original story, not based on any manga, all fans could do was wait patiently to find out what would happen next in Yuri Katsuki and Victor Nikiforov’s careers as ice skaters, especially since the latter decided to continue being a coach.

In April 2017, less than a year after the anime’s premiere, MAPPA announced a prequel movie, following Victor’s career as an ice skater, was under production for a while and even released a teaser. Fans kept waiting years for the anime to return, but their hopes were crushed when MAPPA officially cancelled it in April 2024. The anime is commemorating its 10th anniversary with several exciting surprises such as new merchandise and Blu-ray releases, but none of the announcements share anything about the anime’s continuation.

Yuri!!! on Ice’s Ending Leaves Room For the Story to Expand

Although the first season’s ending was fairly conclusive , it also opens up the door for the story’s expansion. During the beginning of the story, Victor was only supposed to coach Yuri for a year before making his comeback. It goes without saying that the entire time Yuri felt guilty as he believed he was holding back his idol from this thriving career. However, the finale changed everything when Yuri missed the gold medal by a margin and won silver instead. Since he wasn’t able to keep his promise to Victor, he requested his idol to keep being his coach for another year, which represented his significant growth compared to the first episode.

Victor didn’t hide his happiness and instead swore to keep coaching for the next five years so Yuri could win as many gold medals as he did. During the ending credits of the anime finale, we see the two performing together, confirming Victor had made a comeback. This implies that the final performance of the anime happens in the near future, possibly after Yuri won his gold medal. The story concludes with Yuri meeting both Victor and Yuri Plisetsky, the winner of the Grand Prix Finale, as they continue their journey. There’s no denying that the ending was satisfying, but it doesn’t change the fact that we could have seen so much more from the characters, especially Yuri winning the gold medal and Victor’s comeback, but now there will never be a chance to see their journey continue.

Yuri!!! on Ice the movie: Ice Adolescence Would’ve Been a Huge Hit

The anime is still in demand ten years after its premiere, which only means fans would have loved to watch the prequel movie in the theatres. However, MAPPA never gave any hope of continuing the anime again after the cancellation. The studio was pretty clear about cancelling the anime without making any promises on working on it again. While they claim that the anime wasn’t as much of a success as fans think, the truth remains that the movie would’ve been a hit regardless. The prequel movie was going to follow Victor’s journey from a young prodigy to becoming a five-time gold medalist at the age of 27, which was nothing short of marvelous.

He won the hearts of countless people all over the world and reached heights rarely achieved in the world of figure skating by anyone. However, after winning five gold medals and trying out almost every technique possible, his passion for ice skating was slowly fading. Victor always loved surprising his audience with new tricks. However, after his popularity soared, there came a time when, no matter what he did, the audience would enjoy it but wouldn’t feel surprised since they always expected Victor to pull off something unique in his performance.

This is also the primary reason that he found a new purpose in his career after watching Yuri’s viral video, in which the 23-year-old perfectly imitated his free skate routine. Victor found a new purpose in his career and decided to take a year off from competitions and work as a coach. However, the story primarily focused on Yuri’s growth while Victor’s role was mostly to support him as his coach, idol, and lover. The anime also had only a few episodes that couldn’t explore such a nuanced character in depth, as it should have. This is all the more reason why a movie centering around his past was necessary since it would have helped fans understand his character depth and see things from his POV.

What are your thoughts on the anime that played such a crucial role in shaping the future of Jujutsu Kaisen’s studio before its cancellation? Do you think it deserved a longer run, or was its cancellation the right decision?

title: Live-Action My Sister's Boyfriend Film Casts Taisuke Niihara
content:
The official website for My Sister's Boyfriend, the live-action film of Amu Meguro 's Midori Loves My Sister ( Onē-chan no Midori-kun or literally My sister's Midori-kun ) manga, announced on Wednesday that Taisuke Niihara (live-action At 25:00 in Akasaka , Young & Fine ) has joined the film's cast as Amamiya, a new assistant producer at the same TV station where Sui's older sister Momo works.

The original manga centers on Sui, a girl in her third year of junior high. She doesn't really get along with her older sister's boyfriend, Midori-kun, since he always treats her like a kid and makes fun of her. But Midori-kun is suddenly asked to be Sui's home tutor, and she suddenly sees an unexpected side of him.

The film has the English title My Sister's Boyfriend , and stars timelesz idol group member Masaki Hashimoto (live-action Summer Complicity ) as Midori Yukishiro, and actress Runa Nakajima (live-action Uchi no Otōto-domo ga Sumimasen ) as Sui Sanae. title: Toshiaki Yamada's Tokyo Duel Manga Ends
content:
Coamix 's Comic Zenon + manga website published the final chapter of Toshiaki Yamada 's Tokyo Duel ( Tokyo Kettō Kanjōsen ) manga on September 23. The final chapter became free to read on Wednesday.

Coamix publishes the manga volumes in English digitally. Comikey also releases the manga and describes the story:

In post-war Japan, a government-funded program of organized violence called the "Tokyo Loop Line Duels" is promoted to maintain law and order—and it works. Representatives from each station on the Yamanote line battle for control of their territory. Any defeat could mean losing family members, friends, money—or worse. Fast-forward to now, in 2020; a new station has opened up. Everyone, including the popular rookie, Koinosuke, is itching to join the fray for the top spot. Will he be victorious? Or will violence consume them all?

Yamada launched the manga on Comic Zenon + in 2020. Coamix will publish the manga's 22nd and final compiled book volume on November 20.

title: Crunchyroll’s Solo Leveling Replacement for Fall 2026 Is Finally Ready to Level Up
content:
Crunchyroll featuring a new anime every season that can be compared to Solo Leveling has become a norm, and the latest one airing this fall proves it is a perfect replacement as it starts its main journey with the second episode. While the summer season had Tomb Raider King as the latest Korean webtoon anime adaptation that followed Solo Leveling ‘s upgrading journey, the fall has Overgeared , which also had an official collaboration with Solo Leveling , leading fans to interpret the new series as carrying the baton of Solo Leveling this season. Despite having the Solo Leveling element in its premise, Overgeared is a series of its own .

The first episode revealed a miserable protagonist deprived of money and good status, seeking them in the game Satisfy, which affects the elements of his real life. With the in-game name Grid, the protagonist pushes himself and ends up acquiring a legendary class status as the successor of a blacksmith, but this brings him back down to level 1. The first episode comically reveals that Grid continues to lose rank as he is still trying to comprehend his status change. By the end of the first episode, however, Grid understands his legendary status, and the second episode of the series has officially started the leveling-up journey that it promised, and it is perfect.

Overgeared Finally Begins Its Protagonist’s Leveling-Up Journey

After taking a while to realize that his class as a Blacksmith isn’t about going off into battle but rather making tools, Grid takes the necessary steps and starts learning the work of a blacksmith from an NPC, with his first task being to chop a thousand pieces of wood. Though it is a task that he finds tedious, due to the precision Grid gains from his class as a blacksmith, it still pushes him to work all night to complete it. Eventually, he also gains a level upgrade through the process. The episode then sees Grid taking on his next main job as a blacksmith.

To make money, Grid begins crafting arrows, hoping to sell them and earn money, and thanks to his skills, Grid ends up making some epic-level arrows as well, giving him more money while also upgrading his level to three. This episode finally sees Grid beginning a journey of redeeming himself and gaining status within the game, thanks to his crafted arrows receiving recognition. In essence, the second episode gives Grid the exposure he requires to gain the level upgrades and recognition that the series has implied, making it feel very similar to Solo Leveling ‘s journey .

However, the anime carries its own essence throughout, and it is all thanks to the protagonist’s uniqueness, which is essentially his shameful nature and his willingness to beg for help. Grid feels like a real-life character who is desperate enough to make it in life and would do anything for it, and even though he has the trick to level up quicker, Grid’s uniqueness doesn’t fade. This is enough to make Solo Leveling and Overgeared worlds apart, given that Jinwoo’s coolness and combat ability are what define him the most, while Overgeared has a protagonist with the opposite personality and a crafting-based ability. Overgeared is a replacement for Solo Leveling on Crunchyroll this fall , but with its own nuances that make it very refreshing.

title: Netflix’s Most Romantic Series of Fall 2026 Makes Its Return With the Perfect Romantic Drama
content:
The Fall 2026 season is here, meaning every major platform is streaming new and returning content, and with Netflix being one of the biggest streaming platforms, it continues to shine this season as well. Recently, Netflix has expanded its reach and emerged as a leading streaming platform in the anime industry. It has done so by streaming many ongoing anime each season, albeit a little later, while also featuring some exclusives that fans won’t find anywhere else. With the Fall 2026 season bringing a wave of new anime, Netflix is streaming many of them, including two exclusives as well.

While JoJo’s Bizarre Adventure ‘s latest part is undoubtedly stealing the spotlight as the Netflix exclusive this Fall, Blue Box , the romantic sports anime, has also arrived this season with a new season, perfectly presenting the autumn vibe with its premiere. Fans of Blue Box have been waiting for the premiere of this season for a while, as it was poised to feature the first official date that fans have been longing to see. The first episode of the series featured Taiki and Chinatsu’s first date, albeit it wasn’t the perfect one. Rather, it featured the perfect clichéd moments of a first date, and before it could come to an end as a sweet date, it ended on a heavy note, reminding fans what this romantic series’ main notion is.

Netflix’s Returning Romantic Series of Fall 2026 Perfectly Captures Its Core Theme

What makes Blue Box a great romantic series on Netflix is that it doesn’t put its romantic element at the forefront; rather, it is a secondary element, proving that romance doesn’t always have to be on screen to make itself felt. Instead, the romantic emotions are portrayed through the characters’ dedication to sports. Chinatsu and Taiki’s dynamic is built around sports, as the latter idolizes the former’s dedication and falls for her commitment to the sport. With this feeling only growing in a mutual way, the series has now finally featured a date between them. However, this isn’t all about romance and sweetness, as both Taiki and Chinatsu are reminded that they have to worry about something even bigger than this: sports.

Taiki is reminded of this through the third-wheeling guy, who bluntly expresses this to Taiki’s face. Though Taiki dwells on the comment, he defiantly says that he can handle both a relationship and his sports, though there is a lot of hesitation in this. But what makes this notion even better is how Chinatsu is presented with this truth even more aggressively. The whole episode subtly introduces a character from Chinatsu’s past, Yumeka, who is revealed to have been her basketball partner in middle school but gave up on it in high school.

The episode ends with Yumeka appearing, and after she sees Chinatsu with Taiki at what is clearly a couple’s spot, she interprets that Taiki is Chinatsu’s boyfriend and nonchalantly says that having a boyfriend means Chinatsu has given up on basketball. With the episode emphasizing for the second time that sports is not a joke and that a relationship can be a hurdle, it highlights the perfect blend of romance and sports. But what makes Chinatsu and Taiki’s dynamic work so well is that they comprehend the sports element more than others, and thus, seeing them figure out their relationship while becoming the best at their respective sports is what will make Blue Box great and emerge as an even more amazing romantic series on Netflix that fans can and should be watching.

title: Monster Hunter Rise Game Sells 20 Million Copies Worldwide
content:
The official X/Twitter account for CAPCOM 's Monster Hunter franchise announced on Friday that the Monster Hunter Rise game has surpassed 20 million copies sold worldwide.

Monster Hunter Rise launched on Nintendo Switch in March 2021 and then launched on PC via Steam in January 2022. CAPCOM released the game on PlayStation 5, PlayStation 4, Xbox Series X|S, Xbox One, Windows, and Xbox Game Pass in January 2023. The Monster Hunter Rise: Sunbreak expansion for the game debuted for Switch and PC via Steam in June 2022, and launched on PS5, PS4, Xbox Series X|S, Xbox One, Windows, and Xbox Game Pass in April 2023.

Monster Hunter Wilds , the latest main game in the franchise , debuted globally on PS5, Xbox X|S, and PC via Steam in February 2025. The game sold over 8 million copies worldwide in its first three days. According to the company, this is the fastest that one of its titles has reached this milestone. As of March 2025, the game had sold 10 million copies worldwide. The game's Monster Hunter Wilds Ascendance expansion will launch in 2027. The game will get a Nintendo Switch 2 release on December 4.
